## Isaac Lab Review Bot

All reviewed code categories look good.

- **PR description:** The title and body match the export-ordering fix, accurately describe the in-process entry-point tests, and make no performance claim requiring measurements.
- **Design and architecture:** Architecture looks good.
- **Scope and over-engineering:** No over-engineering issues.
- **API:** API changes look good.
- **Compatibility and deprecation:** No breaking changes identified.
- **Implementation:** Implementation looks good.
- **Style consistency:** Style consistency looks good.
- **Test quality:** Test quality looks good.

**No blocking issues.** No inline findings.

_Automated review; human maintainers own approval decisions._

<!-- isaaclab-review-bot:sha=4f703cee0b3e2b739f1fd5d1582d1163b3a51adb -->

The production fix addresses #8969. I verified the real CLI discovery path followed by LEAPP export on CPU: the math helper remains a Python function, validation passes, and inputs `[0.0, 0.5, 1.0]` produce ONNX outputs `[0.5, 0.75, 1.0]` rather than a constant target. This was helper/action-buffer export, not a complete simulator/checkpoint export.

The explicit export-only preparation is proportionate here and preserves centralized discovery. Keeping the guard in `run_export_cli()` also protects callers that bypass the root CLI; no broader dispatch refactor is needed for this fix.

**Please fix the test isolation before merging.** I independently reproduced the existing [inline finding](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/pull/8970#discussion_r4502020404). The new test file passes alone (`3 passed`), but this same-process sequence gives `1 passed, 1 failed`:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  'source/isaaclab/test/cli/test_installed_workflow_entrypoints.py::test_cli_subcommand_dispatches_and_propagates_status[leapp-export]' \
  source/isaaclab/test/cli/test_leapp_entrypoint.py::test_train_still_compiles_helpers_imported_by_external_tasks
```

The training test fails at line 62 with `AssertionError: assert not True`. The existing mocked export-dispatch test now executes the real early JIT disable without restoring it. `_task_helper_stays_python()` preserves the incoming state but does not establish an enabled starting state, so the training check depends on test order and the export check can pass without exercising the new disable.

Please establish a known JIT-enabled precondition and restore the original state, and contain the existing routing test's new global side effect, or isolate these checks in fresh subprocesses. Then rerun the combined sequence. This is a test-state problem, not evidence that fresh-process training is broken.

review_comments.body: **CLI tests fail together** The existing `leapp-export` case in `test_installed_workflow_entrypoints.py` now reaches `torch.jit._state.disable()` without restoring its state. When that case runs first, this helper starts with TorchScript disabled. The new training test then receives the original function and fails despite correct training behavior. Enable TorchScript after saving its state and before calling `cli.cli()`, then keep the existing restoration. ```suggestion enabled = bool(torch.jit._state._enabled) try: torch.jit._state.enable() ```

Confidence Score: 4/5

**[Medium impact]** The change affects task imports in the LEAPP export workflow\. Fix the shared TorchScript state in the new tests before merging.

Findings

1.  **CLI tests fail together** ▶

Summary

Disables TorchScript before external tasks load for `isaaclab leapp export`. - LEAPP export keeps task helpers in Python for tracing. Reviews (1) · Last reviewed commit: ["fix: disable TorchScript before LEAPP ex..."](https://github.com/isaac-sim/isaaclab/commit/4f703cee0b3e2b739f1fd5d1582d1163b3a51adb) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=isaac-sim/isaaclab)

Thanks for reproducing this. The helper in `test_leapp_entrypoint.py` now sets a known JIT-enabled starting state (still restoring the original afterwards), and the existing `leapp-export` routing test restores the TorchScript state it changes. With `isaaclab.sim` stubbed (no simulator install), the combined sequence from the review now gives 2 passed, and 3 passed with the export test added after it. With the CLI change reverted, that export test now fails in the same sequence, so it exercises the new disable.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
